answer.answer: Chevron acquired Hess Corporation on July 18, 2025, for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $48 billion, including 15.38 million Hess shares bought in open market transactions in the first quarter of 2025 and 301.25 million Chevron shares issued as closing consideration in July [1]. As part of the transaction, Chevron assumed debt with an aggregate outstanding principal value of $8.8 billion [1]. The shares issued represented approximately 15 percent of Chevron common stock outstanding immediately after the transaction closed [1]. The acquisition was accounted for as a business combination under ASC 805, and as a result of measuring assets and liabilities at fair value, no goodwill or bargain purchase was recognized [1]. Hess's legacy reserves are reviewed by legacy Hess staff with input from Chevron's RAC, and DeGolyer and MacNaughton audited the legacy Hess proved reserves, which represent approximately 13 percent of Chevron's total proved reserves [2]. Chevron states that realizing the anticipated benefits of the acquisition depends on achieving run-rate cost synergies, estimated five-year production and free cash flow growth rates, and higher long-term shareholder returns, and that failure to do so may have an adverse impact on its financial results [3].

answer.answer: On September 8, 2025, PTFI experienced an external mud rush incident at the Grasberg minerals district that resulted in seven fatalities [1]. Approximately 800,000 metric tons of wet material entered the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine and traveled rapidly to multiple levels of the mine, including a service level where seven team members were later found deceased [2]. Mining operations were temporarily suspended to prioritize recovery of the fatally injured team members and to conduct investigations [1]. In late October 2025, PTFI restarted operations at the unaffected DMLZ and Big Gossan underground mines, and a phased restart and ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine is anticipated to begin in second-quarter 2026 [1]. PTFI expects approximately 85% of its total production at normal operating rates to be restored in the second half of 2026 [3]. PTFI is seeking recovery of damages under its property and business interruption insurance policies, which cover up to $1.0 billion in losses, subject to a $0.7 billion limit on underground incidents, after a $0.5 billion deductible [1].
